name: Luna T7 cryptographic module
description: Half-height PCIe cryptographic module, part 872-500025-001 (Luna T7) and 875-500025-002 (Luna T7U), firmware 7.15.1, bootloader 2.0.1 and 2.0.2 (security policy, table 2). It is built into the Luna PCIe HSM, Luna Network HSM, Luna as a Service and CipherTrust Manager offerings.
comment: Product record of the Thales Luna T7 cryptographic module, firmware 7.15.1, written by the PKIC CBOM Profiles Working Group from the CMVP certificate #5450 and the module's FIPS 140-3 security policy, read on 26 November 2026. Not reviewed by the vendor. Facts the security policy does not state are marked unknown. Built by drafts/hsm-luna-t7/build.py.

interfaces.name: Cryptographic services for host applications over PCIe (ICD commands)

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: The application chooses the mechanism in each command

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: The approved mode must be set by the Security Officer with HSM policy 12 (security policy, section 11.1.2); the module is valid only when configured that way. ICD input and output are plaintext over the PCIe bus (table 18). The user password is entered encrypted under the module's RSA-4096 PEC key (tables 18, 20, 21). Approved services include ML-KEM key generation, encapsulation and decapsulation, ML-DSA and LMS key generation, signing and verification (tables 4, 5 and 13; algorithm certificates A7879 and A7880). Parameter sets are not restated here.

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)

interfaces.name: Administration by the Security Officer and Crypto Officer (ICD commands)

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: Fixed by the firmware; HSM policies set by the Security Officer

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: The approved mode must be set by the Security Officer with HSM policy 12 (security policy, section 11.1.2); the module is valid only when configured that way. Roles authenticate with a password or with PED keys (section 11.1.2, tables 13 and 18).

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)

interfaces.name: PIN entry device for role authentication and the master key split

attributes.name: protocol
values: Luna PED (local serial or remote PED)

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: The PED tunnel is established with KAS-ECC (table 13). Remote PED traffic is protected with KTS-RSA and KTS-HMAC; a locally connected PED (TPED) passes data in plaintext over the serial port (table 18). The SRV, from which the master key is derived together with an internal split, is held on the purple PED key (section 7.7.1, table 21). The curve and the RSA key size of the remote path are not restated.

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)

interfaces.name: Firmware load and its signature check

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: A firmware load test verifies an RSA 4096 signature with SHA2-384 before the new firmware is accepted (table 23). The bootloader checks its own integrity with a SHA-1 error detection code, and the firmware with a SHA2-256 known-answer test (table 22, section 5.1). Whether the verification key can itself be replaced is not stated.

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)

interfaces.name: Cloning of keys between Luna modules

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: The cloning tunnel is established with KAS-RSA between the modules' RSA-4096 TUK keys, whose certificates (TWC) are signed by the module's HOK (tables 13, 20, 21). Objects are wrapped with AES KWP under a cloning key encryption vector derived with a two-step KDF of SP 800-56C and SP 800-108 (section 2.10.2). Only modules in the same domain can clone. No post-quantum key establishment is listed for this interface.

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)

interfaces.name: Key export, import, backup and restore under a wrapping key

attributes.name: algorithmSelection
values: The application chooses the wrapping mechanism

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Key export and import, and partition backup and restore, use KTS-AES (table 13). Approved key transport is AES-KW and AES-KWP (SP 800-38F), RSA-OAEP (SP 800-56B rev 2, 128-bit strength), and AES-CBC with HMAC-SHA2-256 (section 2.10.3). Wrapped keys pass through the WICD path (table 18). ML-KEM is an approved service of the module, but its use for key transport on this interface is not stated.

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)

interfaces.name: Master tamper key in battery-backed NVRAM

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: The MTK, an AES-256 key, is held in battery-backed NVRAM inside the tamper-responsive boundary and is zeroised on tamper or decommission (tables 17, 19, 20, 21). It is derived from an internal split and the SRV held on the purple PED key (section 7.7.1).

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)

interfaces.name: Partition keys in flash, encrypted under the master tamper key

attributes.name: integrationConstraints
values: Partition symmetric, RSA, ECDSA, DSA, LMS, ML-DSA and ML-KEM private keys are stored encrypted in flash and in RAM, under the MTK (section 7.7.1, tables 20 and 21). The wrapping mode is not restated.

attributes.name: moduleValidationRef
values: CMVP certificate #5450 (FIPS 140-3, overall level 3, validated 29 July 2026)
